key_insight: The paper presents a reduced-order model that captures two-way coupling between wind-farm wakes and gravity waves through a dynamic boundary condition at the capping inversion.
engineering_relevance: This provides a computationally efficient way to predict how atmospheric stratification alters farm-scale blockage and wake recovery, which is useful for wind-farm design and performance assessment.
method: Linearize the non-hydrostatic Boussinesq equations for the boundary layer and free atmosphere.
Use a dynamic coupling condition at the capping inversion to exchange pressure and wave effects between regions.
Apply a mixed spectral–finite-difference discretization to retain vertical structure with low computational cost.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated against large-eddy simulations and reproduced both internal wind-farm flow and large-scale gravity-wave effects.
watch_item: Because it relies on linearization and reduced-order assumptions, accuracy may degrade for strongly nonlinear stratification, complex terrain, or conditions outside the modeled boundary-layer regime.
paper_title: Two-way coupling of gravity waves and wind farm wakes: a reduced-order boundary-layer model
